avatar_models.name: HeyGen Avatar 4
avatar_models.max_duration: Not stated in schema or guide; output follows the audio length.
avatar_models.cost_params: talking_style (stable|expressive). aspect_ratio. Resolution is fixed at 1080p, so there is no cheaper tier.
avatar_models.notes: No avatar or voice id needed, only an image and an audio file. No model-specific guide exists.

avatar_models.name: Creatify Aurora
avatar_models.inputs: image (required) + audio (required). The guide mentions an optional visual-context text prompt and a prompt_guidance param (0-4), but neither appears in the schema.
avatar_models.max_duration: Guide says it supports long-form audio, several minutes of continuous speech or singing. No hard limit given.
avatar_models.aspect: No aspect_ratio param, so it probably follows the input image. Resolution 480p or 720p.
avatar_models.cost_params: resolution (480p|720p), guidance_scale and audio_guidance_scale (exposable, any value).
avatar_models.notes: Built for talking heads (UGC ads, podcast clips). The prompt describes the scene, not the speech. Works with ElevenLabs voices directly. An 'avatar' node type exists for a user-picked Avatar+Style image, but only the user can place it via the canvas Avatar Picker. Aurora does not require one: any image works.

avatar_models.name: OmniHuman 1.5
avatar_models.aspect: No aspect param, so it likely follows the image. Resolution 720p or 1080p (default 1080p).
avatar_models.notes: Animates a still image with audio. Needs a well-lit, front-facing image and clear audio.

avatar_models.name: Veed Fabric 1.0
avatar_models.notes: Cheap, fast image-plus-audio talking head. The guide groups it with the lipsync family.

avatar_models.name: MiniMax H3 Max Lip Sync
avatar_models.max_duration: Audio must be 5-14.8s, and output length equals audio length. Longer audio is rejected, so split it into clips and stitch them.
avatar_models.aspect: Output snaps to the nearest standard ratio (9:16, 3:4, 1:1, 4:3, 16:9, ~21:9) based on the image. The image must be at least 256x256 with aspect ratio 0.4-2.5. Resolution 480p, 768p (default), 1080p, 2K.
avatar_models.cost_params: resolution is the main driver. 480p costs about 5/8 of 768p, 1080p about 2x, 2K about 4x. enable_transcription has no visible effect, so leave it off. An image with no face is still charged.
avatar_models.notes: Use one speaker per image. Works on illustrations and animals too. The mouth stays closed during silence.

avatar_models.name: Sync 3
avatar_models.aspect: Follows the input video. No aspect or resolution params.
avatar_models.cost_params: sync_mode (cut_off|loop|bounce|silence|remap) sets how mismatched audio and video lengths are handled. Cost params are otherwise not exposed.
avatar_models.notes: Dubbing and re-lip-sync of an existing video, not generation from a photo.

avatar_models.name: Sync Lipsync 2 Pro
avatar_models.notes: Older Sync version with the same interface.

avatar_models.name: Veed Lipsync
avatar_models.aspect: Follows the input video. No params.

avatar_models.name: Veed Lipsync 2.0
avatar_models.aspect: Follows the input video. No params.
avatar_models.notes: Same interface as Veed Lipsync, newer version.

avatar_models.name: Runway Act-Two
avatar_models.inputs: image (required) + driving performance video (required). No audio input.
avatar_models.notes: Transfers the performance (face and optionally body) from a driving video onto the image subject. It is not audio-driven. The guide describes it as 'Performance / lipsync re-targeting', but its schema has no audio port.

avatar_models.name: LTX Audio-to-Video
avatar_models.notes: General audio-reactive video that syncs to the audio. It is not a dedicated talking-head model.

voice_cloning: No tool or model for instant voice cloning from an uploaded audio sample is available. Voice creation is design-only: creative_design_voice plus creative_save_designed_voice, and the 'voice-creation' node (eleven_ttv_v3) both work from a text description, with no audio input. creative_list_voices only picks existing voices, and I did not call it, so I can't say whether the account already holds cloned voices. The closest substitute is the Voice Changer node (eleven_multilingual_sts_v2). It takes uploaded audio and re-renders it in an existing voice_id, keeping the emotion and timing. That converts speech into a library voice; it does not clone the uploaded speaker. TTS (eleven_v4, v3, multilingual_v2, turbo_v2_5, flash_v2_5) needs a voice_id. Audio can be uploaded via creative_create_asset_upload for transcription, voice changing, isolation, or as lip-sync input. Nothing was generated.
